title: Custom vHost

# Custom vHost

The **vHost** tab shows the website’s full Nginx configuration and lets you rewrite it when you need rewrite rules, headers or special locations.

## Default and custom

The badge at the top of the tab shows the state:

* **Default**: configuration generated by the panel. Changes in the [Overview](overview-tab.md) and [SSL](ssl.md) tabs update it automatically.
* **Custom**: after you save content that differs from what the panel generates.

## Editing the configuration

1. Edit the text in the **Configuration** field.
2. Click save.

The panel validates with `nginx -t` before applying. If Nginx reports an error, **the running configuration is kept** and the detailed error appears on the page. The maximum size is shown under the field.

Caution

If the website has SSL, keep the `location /.well-known/acme-challenge/` block so the Let’s Encrypt certificate can renew.

## Limits of a hand-written configuration

Nginx opens log files as root before it switches to the worker account, so the panel checks a hand-written configuration further (from 1.2.0):

* `access_log` and `error_log` may write only to a file in `/var/log/mpn/sites/<website>/` (or `off`, `stderr`, `syslog:`).
* Directives that read other files or affect the whole machine are refused: `include` (except Nginx’s and the panel’s parameter files), `load_module`, `ssl_certificate` outside the website’s certificate folders, `*_temp_path`, `*_cache_path`, `user`, `pid` and similar.

The panel names the line it refuses. A website whose existing hand-written configuration breaks these limits reports an error at its next apply until you fix that line.

## While a custom configuration is active

These changes are **not applied automatically** to a hand-written configuration, and the panel refuses them until you go back to the default:

* changing the domain,
* enabling or removing SSL,
* changing the HTTPS redirect.

Let’s Encrypt renewal keeps working.

## Resetting to default

While the vHost is custom, a **Reset to default configuration** section appears at the bottom of the tab. Its button discards the hand-written configuration and lets the panel regenerate it. Your custom text is lost, so copy it elsewhere first if you still need it.
